front: What is Functional programming in one sentence?
back: Compose pure functions and immutable data — minimize shared mutable state; side effects at the edges.

front: Explain the mental model of Functional programming (how the system thinks).
back: Core ideas: pure functions (same input → same output), immutability, first-class functions, referential transparency. State changes via new values, not mutation. Higher-order functions (map, filter, reduce) replace many loops. IO/monads/effects pushed to boundaries ("functional core, imperative shell").

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Functional programming?
back: input → f(g(h(x))) → output → no hidden globals; mutation → new copy

front: Given a broken Functional programming setup, what is your first validation command?
Gotcha with Functional programming: what silently fails?
back: map without return — accidental undefined array. Shallow copy nested objects — still aliased inner fields. FP in JS without types — easy to pass wrong arity; use TS.

front: When should you NOT use Functional programming?
back: Don't clone huge graphs every tick in hot paths — profile first. Don't ban all mutation in low-level perf code (games, codecs) — isolate instead.

front: Design a minimal correct Functional programming setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: input → f(g(h(x))) → output

front: What is Purely declarative in one sentence?
back: Describe what result you want; runtime chooses how — SQL, regex, HTML/CSS, Prolog-style rules.

front: Explain the mental model of Purely declarative (how the system thinks).
back: Imperative: step-by-step mutations. Declarative: state the desired outcome or relation. Engine optimizes execution (query planner, layout engine, regex NFA). You trade control of execution order for brevity and optimization headroom — until you need hints (INDEX, EXPLAIN, CSS !important).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Purely declarative?
back: Imperative: loop rows, if age>30, append name → Declarative: SELECT name FROM users WHERE age > 30

front: Given a broken Purely declarative setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Imperative: loop rows, if age>30, append name

front: Symptom: Slow SQL — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: EXPLAIN · Fix: Indexes; rewrite joins; stats vacuum

front: Symptom: Wrong CSS layout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: DevTools box model · Fix: Change declarative props, not manual pixel nudge loops

front: Symptom: K8s drift — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl diff · Fix: GitOps reconcile; fix manifest not pods by hand

front: Symptom: Regex catastrophic backtrack — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Pattern review · Fix: Possessive groups; RE2 engine

front: Symptom: "Can't express logic" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Leaky abstraction · Fix: Escape to imperative UDF/script

front: Gotcha with Purely declarative: what silently fails?
back: Pure declarative myth — hints, pragmas, and $where re-introduce imperative. SQL injection — declarative strings still need parameterization. CSS specificity wars — declarative cascade fights predictability.

front: When should you NOT use Purely declarative?
back: Don't use declarative DSL for procedural algorithms (sort implementation) — use a general language. Don't SQL everything in app strings — ORM/query builder for structure + safety.

front: Design a minimal correct Purely declarative setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: Imperative: loop rows, if age>30, append name
